title_formula_note: Chosen: the CD's working title, 'Why [X] Is Deadlier Than [Y]' (T9 single-animal 'Why X...' family, which sits on the style bible's T6 'Why [X] Gets Deadlier...' skeleton; logged as T9 for formula tracking, like 021). Rule check: (1) 44 chars, 9 words; (2) Title Case, no caps words, emoji, ! or ?; (3) T6/T9 'Why [X] ... Deadlier'; (4) one dread word, 'Deadlier', no death verb; (5) scope device 'Than Any Bear'; (6) no 'in N Minutes', no leading count; (7) shares no word with the planned thumbnail text 'WRONG ANIMAL'; (9) 5 candidates; (10) not a Paint Explainer title or noun swap. Doug is in the title. Honest: 'to Doug' is kept (CD decision 2026-10-21) because ADF&G supports more injuries, not more deaths; Doug dies to moose 8 times and to bears 0 times, and the boss gives the sourced road deaths plus the honesty line. Not T1 or T2. Alternates: (T9) the CD-approved fallback 'Why Moose Hurt More People Than Bears' with a death verb added so it passes rule 4, the most literal claim and the best A/B test against the lead; (T6) 'Nothing About X Is Normal' extended with a death-verb clause so it isn't a noun swap of the PE phrase; (T8) 'Every Way...', distinct from 018's 'Every Reason'; (T4) revelation clause, every habit is from agency or biologist records (Peterson, Mech, ADF&G). Rejected: 'The Deadliest Animal in Alaska Isn't the Bear' (sources don't back 'deadliest'), anything with 'Terrifying... Here's Why' or 'Weirdest' (OctoLab), 'Animal' or 'Wrong' in any title (thumbnail text).

description:
Moose look like gentle giant deer that eat twigs, yet in Alaska they injure more people every year than bears do. Doug finds out why, one moose trait at a time, from the calving season and the autumn rut to deep snow, railway lines and Newfoundland's night roads.

Which animal with a gentle reputation should Doug misjudge next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you're here for Doug's next bad idea.
